title: `mean` of floats on the streaming engine: varies between runs when grouped
verdict: f64 sum / n; grouped, the order of the additions varies between runs
description: On the streaming engine `mean` is `NumMeanReducer`: an `f64` sum and a count. A morsel adds its `_sum_as_f64`, a grouped row adds itself, and pipelines merge by adding sums and counts. A `Float32` mean is the `f64` quotient rounded to `f32`.

The grouping of the additions follows the scheduling of morsels, so a grouped mean can change between runs: one `Float64` group of 1e16, 1, 1, -1e16 gave 0.5, 0.25 and 0.0 on different runs (in memory, Kahan: 0.5). A frame of 2 to 4 rows streams as one-row morsels on a 10-thread machine, so which pipelines add which rows, and in what order their partial sums merge, changes between runs. Its sum takes the same additions as polars-sum-float-streaming's (2.0, 1.0 or 0.0 over 200 runs; always 0.0 with `POLARS_MAX_THREADS=1` or 2), so the mean is that sum divided by 4; the mean's own counts were not recorded. The recorded s-group-mean-cancel (`differ` 0, streaming 0.5) is one outcome among several. The in-memory engine's algorithms are in polars-mean-float.

Order class (streaming): (a) `NumMeanReducer` keeps an `f64` sum: ungrouped, each morsel adds its `_sum_as_f64` (pairwise per chunk) and pipelines merge in turn; grouped, each row is added in turn per pipeline and the pipelines' sums merge; one division by the count, rounded to `f32` for `Float32`. (b) Any tree: γ_{h+1} Σ|x_i| / n, h as in polars-sum-float-streaming, at most n − 1 (Higham §4.2), u = 2⁻⁵³; `Float32` adds one rounding at 2⁻²⁴. (c) The source below; s-group-mean-cancel (0.25 and 0.0 on different runs). (d) `Float64`: ANY. `Float32`: the `f64` sum of the widened values refines ANY, and the final rounding to `f32` is outside `AggFn.avg`.
The docs are silent on the summation order, its variation between runs and the `f64` sum of a `Float32` mean: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the streaming summation order; it may change between versions.
reference: `AggFn.avg` is `floatAvgCR` (D25): the exact sum of the doubles divided by the count, rounded once; non-finite values as for `SUM`. NULL without values. An engine's sum divided by n is within the plan's bound (`sum_order`, `StdModel.epsilon_avg_cr`).

notes: s-group-mean-cancel: 0.5 in memory; streaming 0.25 in the recorded run and 0.0 in another, so the result depends on the run.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each observation (`STREAMING_OBSERVATIONS`, python/tools/sverify_dev/probe_polars.py) with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')` and records both results. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

Corrected (thread-count runs): s-group-mean-cancel's recorded differ 0 (streaming 0.5) is one outcome among several; on 10 threads the streaming mean varies by run, and one or two threads give the sum 0.0.
Carried over from polars-mean-float's round-2 reading. The `Float32` row rests on it: the probes ran `Float64` only.

evidence.note: finish: f64 sum / count, cast to f32 for Float32
NumMeanReducer: reduce_ca adds _sum_as_f64, reduce_one and combine `+=`
ungrouped: one state per pipeline, merged in pipeline order
grouped: reduce_one per row; combine_subset merges the pipelines' states
Higham, Accuracy and Stability of Numerical Algorithms (2nd ed., SIAM 2002), ch. 4 Summation: §4.2 recursive, pairwise and any-order bounds; §4.3 compensated summation
silent on the summation algorithm, run-to-run variation and Float32 handling; engine-support in-memory, streaming, distributed
streaming `mean().over()` compared with in memory under `check_exact=False`: the test suite tolerates rounding differences. No test pins the streaming order
